formulas.name: Mass by volume percentage
formulas.tex: ext{w/V \%} =  rac{	ext{g of solute}}{	ext{mL of solution}} 	imes 100
formulas.where: grams of solute per 100 mL of solution

formulas.name: Parts per million
formulas.tex: ext{ppm} =  rac{	ext{parts of component}}{	ext{total parts}} 	imes 10^6

formulas.name: Molality
formulas.tex: m =  rac{n_{	ext{solute}}}{w_{	ext{solvent}}\,(	ext{kg})} =  rac{w_2 	imes 1000}{M_2 	imes w_1}

formulas.name: Henry's law
formulas.where: $p$ partial pressure of the gas above the solution, $x$ its mole fraction in solution
formulas.units: $K_H$ in pressure units (bar, kbar, mm Hg, Pa)
formulas.note: Higher $K_H$ = lower solubility; $K_H$ rises with temperature

formulas.name: Raoult's law (volatile components)
formulas.tex: p_1 = x_1 p_1^\circ, \qquad p_2 = x_2 p_2^\circ

formulas.name: Total vapour pressure (ideal binary)
formulas.tex: p_{	ext{total}} = x_1p_1^\circ + x_2p_2^\circ = p_1^\circ + (p_2^\circ - p_1^\circ)\,x_2

formulas.name: Ideal solution conditions
formulas.note: Positive deviation: both > 0. Negative deviation: both < 0.

formulas.name: $K_f$ and $K_b$ from thermodynamics
formulas.tex: K_f =  rac{R M_1 T_f^2}{1000\,\Delta_{fus}H}, \qquad K_b =  rac{R M_1 T_b^2}{1000\,\Delta_{vap}H}
formulas.where: $M_1$ molar mass of solvent; temperatures of the pure solvent in K

formulas.name: van't Hoff factor
formulas.tex: i =  rac{	ext{normal molar mass}}{	ext{abnormal molar mass}} =  rac{	ext{observed colligative property}}{	ext{calculated colligative property}}

formulas.name: Colligative properties with $i$
formulas.tex: rac{\Delta p_1}{p_1^\circ} =  rac{i\,n_2}{n_1}, \;\; \Delta T_b = iK_bm, \;\; \Delta T_f = iK_fm, \;\; \pi = iCRT

terms.def: A homogeneous mixture of two or more components whose composition and properties are uniform throughout.
A solution containing two components.
The solvent is usually the component present in the largest amount and decides the physical state; the other components are solutes.
Number of moles of solute dissolved in one litre of solution.
Number of moles of solute per kilogram of solvent.
Moles of a component divided by the total moles of all components.
Number of parts of a component per million parts of all components of the solution (used for trace amounts).
The maximum amount of a substance that can be dissolved in a specified amount of solvent at a specified temperature.
A solution in dynamic equilibrium with undissolved solute, in which no more solute can be dissolved at the same temperature and pressure.
At constant temperature, the solubility of a gas in a liquid is directly proportional to the partial pressure of the gas above the liquid; or $p = K_H x$.
A painful, dangerous condition in divers: dissolved N$_2$ forms bubbles in blood when pressure falls on surfacing, blocking capillaries.
Low blood oxygen at high altitude, where the partial pressure of O$_2$ is low; causes weakness and inability to think clearly.
The pressure exerted by the vapour of a liquid in equilibrium with the liquid at a given temperature.
For a solution of volatile liquids, the partial vapour pressure of each component is directly proportional to its mole fraction in the solution.
A solution that obeys Raoult's law over the entire range of concentration; $\Delta_{mix}H = 0$ and $\Delta_{mix}V = 0$.
A solution that does not obey Raoult's law over the entire range of concentration; its vapour pressure is higher (positive deviation) or lower (negative deviation) than predicted.
A binary mixture having the same composition in liquid and vapour phase and boiling at a constant temperature; it cannot be separated by fractional distillation.
Formed by solutions with large positive / large negative deviation from Raoult's law (ethanol-water / nitric acid-water).
A property that depends on the number of solute particles, irrespective of their nature, relative to the total number of particles in the solution.
$(p_1^\circ - p_1)/p_1^\circ$; equal to the mole fraction of the solute.
Molal elevation constant: the elevation of boiling point produced by a 1 molal solution of a non-volatile non-electrolyte; unit K kg mol$^{-1}$.
Molal depression constant: the depression of freezing point produced by a 1 molal solution of a non-volatile non-electrolyte; unit K kg mol$^{-1}$; $K_f = R M_1 T_f^2/(1000\,\Delta_{fus}H)$.
The temperature at which the vapour pressure of the substance in its liquid phase equals its vapour pressure in the solid phase.
A membrane that lets solvent molecules pass but hinders solute molecules (pig's bladder, parchment, cellophane, cellulose acetate).
The flow of solvent through a semipermeable membrane from pure solvent (or dilute solution) into a solution (or more concentrated solution).
The excess pressure that must be applied to a solution to prevent osmosis, i.e. to stop solvent passing through a semipermeable membrane into it.
Solutions having the same osmotic pressure at a given temperature; no osmosis occurs between them.
A solution with higher / lower osmotic pressure than another (e.g. more / less than 0.9% NaCl relative to blood cells).
Flow of pure solvent out of a solution through a semipermeable membrane when a pressure larger than the osmotic pressure is applied to the solution side; used for desalination.
An experimentally determined molar mass that is lower (dissociation) or higher (association) than the normal value.
Ratio of normal to abnormal molar mass, or of observed to calculated colligative property; $i > 1$ for dissociation, $i < 1$ for association.
